title: Logo Minimum Sizes
slide_intent: Set size thresholds per asset because a complete logo, a wordmark and an abbreviation lose legibility at different scales.
strategic_value: Separate thresholds can keep Burger King recognizable without asking one asset to work below its useful size.
demonstration: Three small specimens compare the small-use logo, wordmark and favicon, each with print-width and digital-width recommendations.
practical_value: Choose the appropriate asset and retain its stated minimum width; remove registration from the primary logo or wordmark at minimum size.

content_islands.name: Minimum-size rationale
content_islands.spec: Place the legibility explanation and registration exception at left.

content_islands.name: Asset comparison
content_islands.spec: Arrange the small-use primary logo, wordmark and favicon across the right, each directly above its dimensional caption.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source says minimum sizes protect impact and legibility; registration becomes too small to read at the minimum logo or wordmark size.
reference_purposes.Application: Recommended widths are logo 0.5 inch/40 pixels, wordmark 1.25 inch/90 pixels, and favicon 0.1875 inch/17.5 pixels.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Remove the registration mark from the primary logo and wordmark when used at minimum size.

ingredient.name: Minimum identity sizes
ingredient.role: Preserve recognition and readable detail at small scales.
ingredient.application: Use recommended widths of 0.5 inch or 40 pixels for the small-use logo, 1.25 inch or 90 pixels for the wordmark, and 0.1875 inch or 17.5 pixels for the favicon.
ingredient.scope: Historical guide; these are width recommendations, not heights. Registration removal applies to primary logo and wordmark at minimum size; approval requirements remain.
